name: chrome-devtools-mcp
one_liner: Lets an AI coding assistant open and inspect a real Chrome browser itself — click around, check performance, read error messages — the same way a human developer debugging a website would.
buyer: No real non-technical buyer. This is a free Google-maintained developer utility, not something a business owner pays for directly.
business_use_cases: A dev agency's AI coding agent uses it to catch and fix visual bugs on a client's site automatically before handoff.
A QA team wires it into CI so AI agents can flag performance regressions on every pull request.
A solo SaaS founder uses it to let their coding agent self-test their web app's checkout flow for bugs before each release.

money_ideas.idea: Build a paid 'automated QA reports' service for small web agencies that packages this tool with a friendly dashboard

steal_this: Honestly, this is pure developer infrastructure with no direct consumer angle. The real business is a layer on top (automated QA-as-a-service), not the tool itself.
